source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Then, the mighty-armed Rama, having dismissed the gold-adorned Pushpaka chariot, entered the Ashoka grove.
verses.2: The grove was beautified all around by sandalwood, aloe wood, and mango trees, as well as tall Kāleyaka trees and forests of Deodar.
verses.3: It was adorned with Champaka, Ashoka, Punnaga, Madhuka, Jackfruit, and Asana trees, and by Parijata trees that shone like smokeless flames.
verses.4: The grove was covered with Lodhra, Nipa, Arjuna, Naga, and Saptaparna trees, Atimuktaka creepers, Mandara trees, banana plants, and dense networks of bushes and vines.
verses.5: It was further adorned by Priyangu, Kadamba, Bakula, Jambu, Pomegranate, and Kovidara trees.
verses.6: The description refers to trees that are always adorned with beautiful flowers, charming fruit, and young sprouts and tender leaves, all possessing divine fragrance and taste.
verses.7: The trees, appearing as if divinely crafted by artisans, were similarly splendid, abundant with beautiful sprouts and flowers, and teeming with intoxicated bees.
verses.8: The place was adorned and made variegated by hundreds of cuckoos, king-bees, and birds of various colors, with mango trees serving as its prominent features.
verses.9: The trees in that place shone with various hues, some resembling refined gold, others like flames of fire, and still others like blue collyrium.
verses.10: There were fragrant flowers and various garlands, along with long ponds of diverse shapes filled with excellent water.
verses.11: The place featured steps crafted from rubies, inner floors paved with crystal, abundant groves of blooming lotuses and water lilies, and was graced by the presence of chakravaka birds.
verses.12: It was filled with the sounds of gallinules, parrots, swans, and cranes, and beautifully adorned by flowering trees growing along its banks.
verses.13: The area was embellished with diverse enclosures and rock surfaces, and within that forest region, there were spots that shimmered like lapis lazuli gems.
verses.14: It was supremely rich with green meadows and flowering tree groves, where trees growing in close proximity were resplendent with blossoms.
verses.15: The rock surfaces were variegated with flowers, resembling the sky adorned with clusters of stars, and indeed, Rama's garden and dwelling were as magnificent as Indra's Nandana or Kubera's Chaitraratha.
verses.16: Indeed, such was Rama's dwelling garden, adorned with numerous seats and pavilions, and enveloped by charming creeper-houses.
verses.17: Having entered the extensive Ashoka grove, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, found a beautifully shaped seat adorned with heaps of flowers.
verses.18: Rama indeed sat down on the seat, which was spread with a mat of Kusa grass, and with Sita by his hand, he had the pure Madhu-Maireyaka wine ready.
verses.19: Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, made her drink, just as Indra makes Shachi drink, and there were well-prepared meats and various fruits.
verses.20: Servants quickly brought food for Rama's meal, and those skilled in dance and song performed before the king.
verses.21: Rama, the best among those who delight, was in the company of young, beautiful, and charming women who were under the influence of drink.
verses.22: Skilled in dance and song, charming women danced before Rama, the best among those who delight.
verses.23: The righteous Rama, always highly adorned, delighted (them), and he shone splendidly while seated with Sita.
verses.24: Rama, filled with joy, thus shone with splendor like Vasishtha seated with Arundhati, with Sita resembling a celestial nymph.
verses.25: Rama, like a god, delighted Sita day after day, and thus Sita and Raghava sported together for a long time.
verses.26: The auspicious and always pleasure-giving winter season, during which Rama and Sita had enjoyed various pleasures, passed away.
verses.27: Having performed his religious duties righteously in the forenoon, the knower of dharma, Rama, spent the remaining half of the day in his inner apartments.
verses.28: Sita also, having performed her morning divine duties, reverently honored all her mothers-in-law without any distinction.
verses.29: Then, adorned with various ornaments and garments, Sita approached Rama, just as Shachi approaches the thousand-eyed Indra seated in heaven.
verses.30: Having seen his wife, Sita, endowed with auspiciousness, Rama felt incomparable joy and exclaimed, "Excellent, excellent!"
verses.31: Rama said to Sita, who had beautiful thighs and resembled a divine daughter, "O Vaidehi, the blessing of progeny has come to me through you."
verses.32: Rama asked Sita, "O one with beautiful thighs, what do you desire? What wish of yours may I fulfill?" Then, smiling, Vaidehi spoke these words to Rama.
verses.33: Sita said, "O Raghava, I desire to see the sacred hermitages and the sages of fierce ascetic power seated on the banks of the Ganga."
verses.34: Sita continued, "O Lord, to dwell at the feet of those who subsist on fruits and roots—this is my greatest desire, that I may be among those who eat roots and fruits."
verses.35: Sita expressed her desire to dwell in a hermitage for even one night, to which Rama, whose deeds were effortless, promised, "So be it, O Vaidehi, be confident, you will undoubtedly go tomorrow."
verses.36: After speaking thus to Sita, Janaka's daughter, Rama, surrounded by his friends, went out to the middle apartment. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 42 ।। Thus ends the forty-second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
